messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] help needed for rstan, related to eigen presumbly
parts:
It looks like a premature typedef in typedefs.hpp. I
think it should be this:

typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,Eigen::Dynamic,Eigen::Dynamic>::Index size_type;

instead of

typedef typename internal::traits<Derived>::size_type size_type;

I think the intention was to have EigenDenseBaseAddons.hpp loaded
first, which I think adds a size_type static variable for matrices.
If that gets loaded first the original typedef would work. But
the one with Index should work eithe way.

Daniel added this flexiblity to allow us to write polymorphic code across
Eigen data structures and std::vector.

I'm running unit tests to confirm that fixing the typedef
doesn't break anything, and it'll hopefully fix your compile problem.
If it persists, we probably have to figure out how to reorder
some more global includes.

I'd prefer to just get rid of the typedef in the stan::math
namespace altogether and be more explicit in uses.

Daniel and I will get together and settle on a standard way
to approach types. The up-and-coming Eigen 3.2 lets you configure
the index type directly, which would let us just standardize
on size_t for indexing everything.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] help needed for rstan, related to eigen presumbly
parts:
On Friday, April 19, 2013 4:16:20 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Daniel and I will get together and settle on a standard way
to approach types.  The up-and-coming Eigen 3.2 lets you configure
the index type directly, which would let us just standardize
on size_t for indexing everything.

It has been configurable for dense matrices since 3.0. But the Eigen people had a long discussion about this and decided that signed types were better, mostly due to avoiding bugs in loops. I don't think there are too many cases in statistical modeling where one wants a matrix whose rows or columns is more than a signed integer can hold. So, I'm not convinced that standardizing on size_t would be a good thing.

Ben

On 4/19/13 8:59 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Friday, April 19, 2013 4:16:20 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
> Daniel and I will get together and settle on a standard way
> to approach types. The up-and-coming Eigen 3.2 lets you configure
> the index type directly, which would let us just standardize
> on size_t for indexing everything.
>
>
> It has been configurable for dense matrices since 3.0. But the Eigen people had a long discussion about this and decided
> that signed types were better, mostly due to avoiding bugs in loops. I don't think there are too many cases in
> statistical modeling where one wants a matrix whose rows or columns is more than a signed integer can hold. So, I'm not
> convinced that standardizing on size_t would be a good thing.

Makes sense to me. I prefer signed to unsigned for just this
reason.

The only bummer is that we have to use the trait-based typedef
whenever we want polymorphism over an Eigen vector/matrix and std
vector. I think we're actually making progress in generalizing
some of this code, so it's not as onerous as it used to be. And
now I'm trying to generalize beyond single dimensional std::vector,
so you lose the shared code again. (So that we can have 2D arrays
get assigned a value and what not.)

- Bob

That would be nice, but I don't think it'll fly. std::vector
uses plain old unsized size_t and as far as I know, there's no
way to configure that. So we'll have to use the
Eigen Index typedef and the std::vector size_type typedef instead.

- Bob
